text: dsh-fastcel 是 DSH Web 插件，为 Vercel AI Gateway 模型请求按近期吞吐量排列 provider，并将顺序交给网关。输入框旁会显示领先 provider；面板展示速度、首 token 延迟、近期可用率及上一条回复的实际 provider。用户也可用 /fastcel 查看指定模型排名或刷新统计。适合希望在 DSH 中优先尝试较快网关 provider 的用户；插件通过公开统计端点查询排名，不需单独配置 API key。

dsh-fastcel ranks Vercel AI Gateway providers by throughput and sets their order on eligible requests. Its composer pick shows the leader; the panel compares speed, latency, uptime, and the provider used for the last reply. Use /fastcel to view or refresh rankings. No plugin key is required.

dsh-fastcel 的功能「Gateway provider 排名」：模型请求时按统计排列 provider 并交给网关；输入框旁显示领先项，打开面板或运行 /fastcel 可查看完整排名。
dsh-fastcel 会向 ai-gateway.vercel.sh 请求模型的 provider 统计端点；该请求携带模型标识用于查询排名，代码中未附加会话内容或插件专用 API key。

dsh-fastcel README · dsh-fastcel：A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugin that starts each Vercel AI Gateway conversation on the fastest provider for its model. It is the harness edition of [fastcel](https://github.com/DavidCarliez/fastcel), the Oh My Pi plugin.

dsh-fastcel README · dsh-fastcel：Vercel AI Gateway serves many models through several providers, and their speeds differ a lot. `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` has 22 providers. On one afternoon the fastest, subconscious, produced a median of 394 tokens per second over the last hour, and the slowest measured, runinfra, 42. Left to choose, the gateway sent three test requests to baseten (175 tok/s). With fastcel the same request went to subconscious.
dsh-fastcel README · How it works：fastcel decides the order in which providers are tried. Vercel decides how long a conversation stays on the provider it landed on.
dsh-fastcel README · fastcel ranks the providers：On every model call the harness sends to `ai-gateway.vercel.sh`, fastcel attaches the model's providers, fastest first:

dsh-fastcel README · fastcel ranks the providers：1. It reads the provider stats from `GET /v1/models/{model}/endpoints`. This is public data, the same figures shown on the model's page at vercel.com/ai-gateway/models, and needs no key. The stats are cached per model for 15 minutes. Once they are stale, requests keep using them while a refresh runs in the background.
2. It orders the providers by median throughput over the last hour. A provider goes to the back of the list when it is deprecated, when fewer than 90% of its requests succeeded in the last 15 minutes, when the request has tools and the provider does not support them, or when its context window is smaller than the conversation.
3. It sends the list as `providerOptions.gateway.order`. If the first provider fails, the gateway falls back through the rest in speed order.

dsh-fastcel README · fastcel ranks the providers：fastcel keeps no ranking between requests: each one carries the ranking as it stands at that moment. If the stats cannot be loaded, the request goes out unchanged and the gateway chooses as usual.

dsh-fastcel README · Vercel keeps a conversation on one provider：The gateway does not simply take the first provider on the list. Its [session affinity](https://vercel.com/docs/ai-gateway/models-and-providers/session-affinity), on by default, remembers which provider answered a conversation's previous message and tries that provider first, so its prompt cache stays warm. In a session this plays out as follows:
section: Vercel keeps a conversation on one provider

text:
dsh-fastcel README · Vercel keeps a conversation on one provider：1. **First message.** No provider is remembered yet, so the message goes to the top of fastcel's list.
2. **Following messages.** They stay on that provider, even if fastcel's ranking changes in the meantime.
3. **After a pause or a failure.** Vercel forgets the provider once the conversation has been idle longer than that provider's cache lifetime: about 5 minutes for most providers, 10 for OpenAI and Azure, and 1 hour for DeepSeek's own API. It also forgets it when the provider fails a request. The next message goes to whichever provider is fastest at that point, and the conversation stays there.
section: Vercel keeps a conversation on one provider

text: dsh-fastcel README · Vercel keeps a conversation on one provider：A new session or a subagent counts as a new conversation, so it starts on whichever provider is fastest when it begins.

text: dsh-fastcel README · How it hooks into the harness：The harness's pi-ai adapter builds the gateway request itself and offers no hook to change its body, so fastcel works at two layers:
section: How it hooks into the harness

text:
dsh-fastcel README · How it hooks into the harness：- An `llm/stream` listener wraps every model call in a request scope that knows the session and how many tokens its conversation held after the previous call.
- A hook on the process's `fetch` changes a request only when it comes from such a scope, is a `POST` to an inference endpoint of `https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh` (`/v1/messages`, `/v1/chat/completions` or `/v1/responses`), and its JSON body names a model. It adds the order, sends the request, and reads the gateway's routing record from the reply as it streams by, unchanged.
section: How it hooks into the harness

text: dsh-fastcel README · How it hooks into the harness：Every other request in the process is forwarded untouched. Stopping the plugin removes the hook.
section: How it hooks into the harness

text:
dsh-fastcel README · Details：- **Routing already in the request wins.** A request whose body already carries `providerOptions.gateway.order` or `.only` is sent as it is.
- **Some providers are skipped for your account.** Vercel marks some providers `plan_not_eligible` for some models. The gateway then moves on to the next provider in the list without trying the skipped one.
- **Why not `sort: "tps"`.** The gateway can sort providers by throughput itself, but when fastcel was tested most providers had no value in that sort, so faster providers came after slower ones; see [fastcel's notes](https://github.com/DavidCarliez/fastcel#details). fastcel ranks with the endpoint stats instead.

dsh-fastcel README · Install：**Requires:** DeepSeek Harness **0.2.1-rc.2** (tested, web profile), Node.js **22+**, and a `vercel-ai-gateway` route on the harness's pi-ai adapter, for example in your profile's `cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- id: llm-pi-ai
  name: "@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-pi-ai"
  config:
    providers:

Any pi-ai route whose endpoint is `https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh` works; fastcel recognizes the gateway by the host each request goes to, not by the route's name.

From this repository, run:

dsh-fastcel README · Install：```sh
npm ci
npm run build
dsh plugin --profile web add "link:$PWD"
```

Then restart the harness. Install, restart or remove the plugin only when no reply is being generated. To remove it, run `dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-fastcel` and restart.

dsh-fastcel README · Use：Pick any Vercel AI Gateway model. fastcel shows the top of its current ranking, the provider and its speed, with a ⚡ in front:

```
⚡ subconscious · 394 tok/s
```

It sits below the composer of a session, and in the options row above the composer on the New Session page. It is hidden when the selected model does not go through the gateway.

dsh-fastcel README · Use：When the model's maker serves it from its own API, that provider has the maker's name, so the panel marks it first-party, and the pick reads `deepseek (first-party) · 191 tok/s`. That means DeepSeek's own API, not the DeepSeek model.

A conversation that started earlier can still be on another provider, as described above. The panel shows where the last reply actually went.

dsh-fastcel README · Use：| Command            | Effect                                                                                                    |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `/fastcel`         | Opens the panel for the session's model. Outside the web client it prints the same table as text.          |
| `/fastcel <model>` | Prints the ranking of any gateway model as a table, e.g. `/fastcel zai/glm-5.1`.                           |
| `/fastcel refresh` | Drops cached stats, fetches them again and prints the session model's ranking.                            |

dsh-fastcel README · Use：Clicking the pick opens the same panel. It lists the model's providers, fastest first, with each provider's speed, time to first token and uptime over the last 15 minutes. A note marks the first-party provider and says why a provider was moved down the list. Under the table, a line says which provider served the session's last reply and what Vercel's session affinity did. While the panel is open it follows replies as they finish. On a phone, the time to first token and uptime columns give way.

dsh-fastcel README · Use：The served-by line comes from the routing record the gateway puts at the end of each reply, so it needs no extra request and no key. fastcel keeps it in memory for the most recent sessions; restarting the harness clears it.

dsh-fastcel README · Develop：```sh
npm ci
npm test
npm run build
npm run check:package

The tests boot the real LLM runtime and pi-ai adapter over a fake network, so they check the request the Anthropic SDK actually sends, with no cloud calls. `check:package` packs the plugin from a clean checkout and loads its host and client entry points. CI runs all three on Node.js 22 and 24.

dsh-fastcel README · Develop：`src/ranking.js` orders providers, `src/stats.js` fetches and caches the endpoint stats, `src/router.js` and `src/gateway.js` change the gateway request and read its routing record, `src/fastcel.js` keeps the per-session state and builds reports, `src/server.js` wires them into the harness, and `src/client.jsx` draws the pick and the panel.

Rebuild after source edits. Client changes reach an open page on reload; host changes need a harness restart.
